public_rationale: On the ordinary dry-powder reading supported by the surrounding discussion, $325 billion did not exceed the world's available private capital. PitchBook reports $4.63 trillion for Q2 2025. A contemporaneous S&P publication also reports a much larger stock within private equity alone. This contradicts the global comparison, while leaving open whether OpenAI could attract the financing it wanted.
limitations: Dry powder consists of investment commitments subject to fund mandates and deployment periods.
The latest completed reporting quarter is used rather than an exact September 29 snapshot.
The decisive historical estimate was published after the post but before the evaluation date.
This does not validate the estimated cost or legal status of the NVIDIA arrangement.

statement.excerpt: The $325 billion it needs just to fulfil its NVIDIA contract, albeit over 4 years, is an egregious sum that I believe exceeds the available private capital in the world.

from_speaker: exceeds the available private capital in the world
our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion of investment firms' available capital makes worldwide private-capital dry powder the ordinary measure: committed capital not yet deployed.
This assesses the comparison with $325 billion, not the separate accuracy of the estimated NVIDIA-related cost.
'Over 4 years' describes the proposed expenditure schedule, not a condition or a four-year forecast of global capital availability.
For the ongoing capital-stock observation, I use Q2 2025, the most recent completed reporting quarter before September 29, 2025.
Available global capital does not mean capital whose owners would be willing or permitted to invest it all in OpenAI.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable worldwide private-capital dry powder in Q2 2025 was below $325 billion.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable worldwide private-capital dry powder in Q2 2025 was at least $325 billion.
